system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: Leo Martins had an interactive logon on WS-LMARTINS-01 shortly before the reviewed interval.

Several connections from WS-LMARTINS-01 went to the internal proxy at 10.40.20.30:8080 during the alert period; the Zeek records show connection timing and byte counts but do not identify the external HTTPS destination or initiating process.

Just after the alert period, the proxy recorded a successful CONNECT to the approved PixelForge update host, and endpoint records attribute the corresponding proxy connection to the approved pfupdater.exe path. This makes benign updater activity plausible, but does not establish the process or destination for earlier connections.
The workstation connected to FILE-NWD-01 over SMB twice; the server recorded both sessions as ANONYMOUS LOGON. The records do not show which shares or operations were involved.

At 14:11 UTC, DC-NWD-01 initiated a connection to the workstation on TCP port 135, and WmiPrvSE.exe subsequently exited. The records do not establish what action occurred or whether these events were related.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor-coverage metadata reports a log-collection outage for WS-LMARTINS-01 winsec and Sysmon, and for the proxy, from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC; that metadata has no record ID.

Because of the reported outage, the available records do not provide endpoint process attribution or proxy CONNECT destinations for the alert-period connections. Zeek records identify the internal proxy endpoint, not the external HTTPS host (for example, T056-00043 and T056-00168).
The proxy and endpoint records available at 14:10:35 UTC are outside the stated outage window and do not by themselves identify the earlier connections (T056-00192 through T056-00195).
claims_not_established: Whether the alert-period proxy connections were all generated by PixelForge pfupdater.exe.
Which external hosts the alert-period connections reached, and whether their content or purpose was benign.
What SMB shares or operations were involved in the anonymous sessions to FILE-NWD-01.
Whether the 14:11 UTC RPC connection and WmiPrvSE.exe exit were authorized administrative activity or related to the alert.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain proxy CONNECT logs for 13:30–14:10 UTC, including destinations, users, and byte counts, and correlate them with the available Zeek connections.
Recover WS-LMARTINS-01 process and network telemetry for the outage interval to identify the process responsible for each proxy connection.
Review FILE-NWD-01 SMB share and object-access auditing for the sessions at 13:55 and 14:03 UTC.
Review DC-NWD-01 and WS-LMARTINS-01 WMI, RPC, and process-creation telemetry around 14:11 UTC, and confirm whether the activity was authorized.
